That describes inline policies.
takeaway: AWS managed policies: AWS-maintained, reusable, not editable.

question: An application needs a configuration value, such as a feature flag, that isn’t secret. Which low-cost option should it use?
options: AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation turned on
Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameters
explanations: Secrets Manager is designed for secrets that need rotation, and it charges per secret.
ACM manages certificates.
KMS manages encryption keys.
Standard parameters store configuration values at no extra cost.
takeaway: Plain configuration values → Parameter Store.

question: Which TWO tasks require signing in as the AWS account root user? (Select TWO.)
options: Changing the root user’s email address
explanations: Any identity with permission can launch instances.
Any identity with permission can create buckets.
Root account settings can be changed only by the root user.
Administrators can create roles.
Closing the account requires the root user.
takeaway: Root-only: account settings, closing the account, and a few others.

question: What happens when no IAM policy allows an action for a user?
options: The action is denied by default (implicit deny)
The action is allowed by default
AWS Support reviews the request and approves or rejects it
The root user is asked to approve it
explanations: Without an explicit allow, requests are denied.
IAM denies by default.
AWS Support isn’t involved in authorization.
IAM doesn’t ask for approvals.
takeaway: No allow → implicit deny.

question: Which of the following is a long-term credential?
options: Session credentials from IAM Identity Center
Credentials returned when assuming an IAM role
explanations: STS credentials expire.
Identity Center sessions are temporary.
Access keys last until they are rotated or deleted.
Role credentials are temporary.
takeaway: Access keys are long-term; roles and Identity Center give temporary credentials.

question: A company wants users to have signed in with MFA before they can delete production resources. Which approach supports this?
options: A Trusted Advisor check for deletes
An AWS Config rule that deletes resources
A CloudWatch alarm that fires when someone deletes a production resource
An IAM policy condition that requires MFA for the delete actions
explanations: Trusted Advisor doesn’t enforce MFA.
Config rules evaluate configurations.
An alarm reports after the fact; it doesn’t block.
Policy conditions can require MFA for specific actions.
takeaway: Require MFA for sensitive actions → IAM policy condition.

question: In IAM Identity Center, how can an administrator give a new hire the same access to three AWS accounts as the rest of the team?
options: Create new access keys for the new hire in each account
Add the new hire to the team’s group, which is assigned permission sets in those accounts
Share the team lead’s sign-in details
Create an IAM user for the new hire in each account and copy the team’s existing policies
explanations: Long-term keys aren’t needed for console access.
Group assignments give consistent access to every member.
Sharing credentials removes accountability.
This bypasses central access management.
takeaway: Consistent access for a team → Identity Center groups + permission sets.

question: Which feature helps a company find IAM roles and users with unused permissions so it can tighten them?
explanations: Access Analyzer’s unused access findings report unused roles, keys, and permissions.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
takeaway: Find unused permissions → IAM Access Analyzer.

question: Which type of policy is attached to a resource, such as an S3 bucket, to control who can access it?
options: A resource-based policy, such as a bucket policy
An identity-based policy attached to an IAM group
explanations: Resource-based policies are attached to the resource.
Identity-based policies attach to users, groups, and roles.
Password policies set password rules.
SCPs apply to accounts in an organization.
takeaway: Policy on the resource → resource-based policy (bucket policy).

question: A company uses AWS Organizations. How can it stop all member accounts from creating resources outside two approved Regions?
options: Turn off the unapproved Regions in the Amazon Route 53 console settings
Attach a service control policy that denies actions in other Regions
Delete the other Regions from each account
explanations: Route 53 is a DNS service.
SCPs set permission limits for all accounts in an OU or organization.
Password policies don’t restrict Regions.
Regions can’t be deleted from accounts.
takeaway: Restrict Regions across accounts → SCP.

question: Which service blocks common web exploits and can rate-limit requests that come from a single IP address?
explanations: GuardDuty detects threats but doesn’t filter requests.
WAF supports managed rules and rate-based rules.
Network ACLs filter by IP and port but can’t rate-limit.
Shield Standard protects against network-level DDoS attacks.
takeaway: Web exploits and rate limiting → AWS WAF.

question: Which TWO data sources does Amazon GuardDuty analyze to detect threats? (Select TWO.)
explanations: GuardDuty analyzes network activity from flow logs.
Artifact reports aren’t threat data.
GuardDuty analyzes account activity in CloudTrail.
Password policies aren’t a GuardDuty data source.
Billing data isn’t used for threat detection.
takeaway: GuardDuty analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and more.

question: Which service can show whether a company’s EC2 instances are reachable from the internet on unintended ports, as part of its vulnerability findings?
explanations: Artifact provides compliance reports.
Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.
Inspector reports software vulnerabilities and network reachability.
Cognito manages app users.
takeaway: Unintended network exposure → Inspector.

question: Which service lets a security team apply security group policies consistently across all accounts in AWS Organizations?
explanations: Security Hub reports findings.
IAM controls API permissions, not security groups across accounts.
Firewall Manager centrally applies security group, WAF, and other policies.
Config can detect noncompliant security groups but doesn’t apply policies.
takeaway: Apply firewall policies across accounts → Firewall Manager.

question: A company wants a Lambda function to run automatically whenever GuardDuty creates a new finding. Which service routes the finding to the function?
explanations: Inspector creates its own findings; it doesn’t route others.
CloudTrail records API calls; it doesn’t route findings.
EventBridge rules can match GuardDuty findings and invoke Lambda.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
takeaway: React to security findings automatically → EventBridge + Lambda.

question: Which TWO AWS security services detect issues rather than block traffic? (Select TWO.)
explanations: GuardDuty detects threats and reports findings.
Inspector detects vulnerabilities and reports findings.
WAF blocks or allows web requests.
Network ACLs allow or deny traffic.
Shield mitigates DDoS attacks.
takeaway: Detect: GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie. Block: WAF, Shield, ACLs.

question: Where can a company find AWS security best practices, whitepapers, and bulletins in one place?
explanations: Marketplace sells third-party products.
The Health Dashboard shows service events.
The Security Center collects AWS security resources and guidance.
The calculator estimates costs.
takeaway: Security guidance hub → AWS Security Center (and Security Blog).

question: Which service offers AWS-managed rules that block known bad bots and requests from IP addresses with a poor reputation?
explanations: GuardDuty detects threats but doesn’t filter web requests.
Shield Standard protects against DDoS attacks.
WAF managed rule groups include bot control and IP reputation lists.
Macie discovers sensitive data.
takeaway: Bot and IP reputation filtering for web apps → AWS WAF.

question: A company’s security team must review AWS’s own security controls before approving a migration. Which TWO resources help? (Select TWO.)
options: The AWS Security Center and its whitepapers
explanations: Cost Explorer analyzes spending.
Trusted Advisor checks the company’s account.
Inspector scans the company’s workloads, not AWS’s controls.
Artifact provides third-party audit reports of AWS controls.
These describe how AWS secures its infrastructure.
takeaway: Learn about AWS’s controls → Artifact reports + Security Center.

question: Which service can scan AWS Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities in their package dependencies?
explanations: Macie discovers sensitive data.
Detective investigates findings.
Inspector scans Lambda functions, EC2 instances, and container images.
GuardDuty detects threats from activity.
takeaway: Vulnerable dependencies in Lambda → Inspector.

question: A company wants to detect when someone makes an S3 bucket public and find out whether that bucket holds sensitive data. Which TWO services help? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Artifact provides compliance reports.
Inspector scans compute workloads.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
Macie evaluates bucket access and discovers sensitive data.
Config rules can flag buckets that allow public access.
takeaway: Public bucket + sensitive data → Config (or Macie) for exposure, Macie for data.

question: A company wants its customer managed encryption keys to be rotated automatically on a schedule. Which service provides this?
explanations: KMS supports automatic rotation of customer managed keys.
With CloudHSM, the customer manages keys and rotation.
Secrets Manager rotates secrets, not KMS keys.
ACM renews certificates, not encryption keys.
takeaway: Automatic rotation of encryption keys → KMS.

question: Which TWO actions help protect data in transit? (Select TWO.)
options: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN between networks
Use HTTPS with TLS certificates from AWS Certificate Manager
explanations: Storage classes affect cost and retrieval.
This protects data at rest.
VPN tunnels encrypt traffic between networks.
TLS encrypts data moving between clients and servers.
Versioning protects against overwrites.
takeaway: In transit: TLS/HTTPS and VPN. At rest: KMS-based encryption.

question: Which statement about AWS Shield Standard is correct?
options: It must be purchased separately with a one-year subscription commitment
It is automatically enabled for all AWS customers at no extra cost
It includes the Shield Response Team
explanations: That describes Shield Advanced.
Every customer gets Shield Standard.
That is AWS WAF.
The response team comes with Shield Advanced.
takeaway: Shield Standard: automatic and free. Shield Advanced: paid, with a response team.

question: A company wants to block requests from specific countries to its website on Amazon CloudFront. Which service should it use?
explanations: Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
Route 53 routes DNS queries; it doesn’t block web requests.
Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.
WAF geographic match rules block requests from chosen countries.
takeaway: Block requests by country → AWS WAF geo match rules.

question: A company wants to store database credentials encrypted and control access with IAM. Which TWO services can store them? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Secrets Manager stores and can rotate secrets.
SecureString parameters are encrypted with KMS.
ACM manages certificates.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
KMS manages encryption keys; it doesn’t store application secrets.
takeaway: Secrets: Secrets Manager (with rotation) or Parameter Store SecureString.

question: A new developer will use both the AWS Management Console and the AWS CLI. Which TWO statements about the credentials involved are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: An EC2 key pair is used to sign API requests to AWS services
A secret access key can be viewed and copied again from the IAM console at any time after it is created
An IAM user signs in to the AWS Management Console with a password, plus MFA when it is set up
AWS CLI and SDK calls are signed with an access key ID and a secret access key
An account ID and an IAM user name are enough to call AWS APIs
explanations: Key pairs are for connecting to instances with SSH, not for calling AWS APIs.
The secret is shown just once, when the key is created.
Console access uses a password and MFA.
Programmatic access uses the access key pair (or temporary credentials that include one).
Identifiers aren’t secrets; API calls need signed credentials.
takeaway: Programmatic → access key ID + secret access key. Console → password (+ MFA). SSH → key pair.

question: An administrator created an access key for an IAM user but closed the window without saving the secret access key. What should the administrator do?
options: Reset the user’s console password to show the secret again
Create a new access key and delete the unused one
Open an AWS Support case to recover the secret access key
Retrieve the secret access key from the IAM console
explanations: Console passwords are separate from access keys.
A lost secret can’t be recovered, so replace the key.
AWS can’t retrieve the secret either.
IAM shows the secret access key just once, when the key is created.
takeaway: Lost secret access key → create a new key and remove the old one.

question: Which TWO statements about protecting data on AWS are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: AWS Certificate Manager provides TLS certificates that encrypt data in transit
AWS Shield encrypts network traffic so that attackers can’t read it during a DDoS attack on the application
AWS KMS manages the keys that services such as Amazon EBS use to encrypt data at rest
AWS Security Hub encrypts data that moves between AWS accounts
Amazon Macie encrypts the sensitive data that it finds in Amazon S3
explanations: ACM certificates enable HTTPS and other TLS connections.
Shield protects availability against DDoS attacks; it doesn’t encrypt data.
KMS creates and controls encryption keys for data at rest.
Security Hub collects security findings and runs compliance checks.
Macie discovers and reports sensitive data; it doesn’t encrypt it.
takeaway: In transit → TLS with ACM certificates. At rest → KMS keys. Shield, Security Hub, and Macie don’t encrypt.

question: A security team must find known software vulnerabilities on its Amazon EC2 instances and identify S3 objects that contain personal data. Which TWO services should it use? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Detective helps investigate findings after they occur.
GuardDuty detects threats from account and network activity, not software vulnerabilities or personal data.
Macie discovers sensitive data such as personal information in S3.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
Inspector scans EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities.
takeaway: Vulnerabilities → Inspector. Sensitive data in S3 → Macie. Threats → GuardDuty. Investigation → Detective.

question: After an outage, an operations team must find out which user deleted a security group and see how the instances’ CPU utilization changed in the hour before. Which TWO services provide this information? (Select TWO.)
explanations: X-Ray traces requests through an application.
CloudWatch stores metrics such as CPU utilization over time.
Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.
CloudTrail records the API call, including who deleted the security group.
Inspector finds software vulnerabilities.
takeaway: Who did it → CloudTrail. How the resource performed → CloudWatch.

question: A company runs an application on AWS Lambda that stores data in Amazon RDS. Which TWO tasks remain the company’s responsibility? (Select TWO.)
options: Patching the operating system and runtime environment that run the Lambda functions
Replacing failed storage hardware under the database
Patching the database engine on the RDS instance
Keeping secrets such as database passwords out of the function code
Controlling which identities and networks can connect to the database
explanations: AWS manages the Lambda execution environment.
AWS maintains the physical infrastructure.
AWS patches the RDS engine during the maintenance window.
Protecting credentials and code is the customer’s job.
IAM, security groups, and database users are configured by the customer.
takeaway: Managed services: AWS patches and runs the platform; the customer controls access, code, and secrets.

question: A company has 12 AWS accounts that each pay a separate bill. It wants one bill for all accounts and a way to stop any account from using unapproved services. Which TWO AWS features should it use? (Select TWO.)
options: An IAM password policy in each account
explanations: SCPs set the maximum permissions for accounts in an organization.
Budgets alerts on spending but doesn’t combine bills or block services.
Password policies set password rules; they don’t restrict services or combine bills.
Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.
Organizations combines the accounts’ charges into one bill.
takeaway: One bill + guardrails across accounts → AWS Organizations (consolidated billing and SCPs).

question: Which TWO findings can AWS Trusted Advisor report in its security checks? (Select TWO.)
options: Security groups that allow unrestricted access to specific ports
Credit card numbers stored in S3 objects
Malware on an EC2 instance’s volumes
An AWS account root user without MFA
Known software vulnerabilities in the container images stored in Amazon ECR repositories
explanations: Trusted Advisor flags rules open to 0.0.0.0/0 on sensitive ports.
Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.
GuardDuty Malware Protection detects malware.
Trusted Advisor checks whether MFA is turned on for the root user.
Amazon Inspector scans container images.
takeaway: Trusted Advisor security checks: open security groups, root MFA, public buckets, exposed keys. Not malware, CVEs, or PII.

question: An application on Amazon EC2 needs to read a DynamoDB table, and 200 employees need to sign in to five AWS accounts with their corporate credentials. Which TWO solutions should the company use? (Select TWO.)
options: IAM Identity Center connected to the corporate identity provider
Long-term access keys stored in the application’s configuration file on the instance
An Amazon Cognito user pool for the employees
An IAM role attached to the EC2 instance
One shared IAM user in each account for the employees
explanations: Employees sign in once and get access to their assigned accounts.
Long-term keys in files can leak; roles provide temporary credentials.
Cognito is for the customers of web and mobile apps, not workforce access to AWS accounts.
The role gives the application temporary credentials automatically.
Shared users break accountability and least privilege.
takeaway: Workloads → IAM roles. Workforce across accounts → IAM Identity Center. App customers → Cognito.

question: Auditors ask a company for AWS’s SOC 2 report and for proof that the company’s own resources follow its tagging and encryption rules continuously. Which TWO services provide this? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Detective investigates security findings.
Inspector finds software vulnerabilities, not compliance reports or configuration rules.
Artifact provides AWS’s compliance reports, such as SOC reports.
Config rules evaluate resource configurations continuously and keep a history.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
takeaway: AWS’s own compliance reports → Artifact. Your resources’ compliance → Config.

question: Which TWO statements about AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: IAM users must be created separately in each AWS Region where they need access
A role provides temporary credentials to the identities that assume it
A new IAM user has no permissions until a policy grants them
IAM charges a monthly fee for each user in the account
IAM groups can contain other IAM groups
explanations: IAM is a global service; users apply in every Region.
Roles issue temporary security credentials.
IAM denies by default.
IAM is offered at no additional charge.
Groups contain users; they can’t be nested.
takeaway: IAM: global, deny by default, groups hold users, roles give temporary credentials, no extra charge.

question: A company stores customer files in Amazon S3. Which TWO tasks are AWS’s responsibility? (Select TWO.)
options: Storing objects redundantly across multiple devices
Choosing which customer managed KMS key encrypts the objects
Deciding whether a bucket can be accessed publicly
Deciding which users can download objects with presigned URLs
Patching the servers and software that run the S3 service
explanations: AWS designs and runs S3’s durable storage.
Encryption choices are the customer’s.
Block Public Access and bucket policies are customer settings.
Access to data is the customer’s responsibility.
AWS maintains the infrastructure behind S3.
takeaway: S3: AWS runs durable, patched infrastructure; the customer controls access and encryption choices.

question: A team must create the same VPC, subnets, and instances in several AWS accounts in a repeatable way. Which approach should it use?
options: Manual setup in the AWS Management Console
Notifications from the AWS Health Dashboard
Infrastructure as code with AWS CloudFormation
explanations: Trusted Advisor recommends improvements; it doesn’t create resources.
Manual setup is slow and inconsistent across accounts.
The Health Dashboard reports AWS events.
Templates create identical environments every time.
takeaway: Repeatable environments → infrastructure as code (CloudFormation).

question: Which tool lets an administrator manage AWS services from a terminal and write scripts to automate tasks?
explanations: The Health Dashboard shows service events.
The CLI runs AWS commands from a terminal and in scripts.
The console is a web interface.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
takeaway: Terminal and scripts → AWS CLI.

question: A developer wants a Python application to upload files to Amazon S3. Which option should the developer use in the application?
explanations: The console is for people, not application code.
SDKs let application code call AWS APIs.
Run Command runs scripts on managed servers.
CloudFormation provisions resources; it doesn’t upload files from an app.
takeaway: Call AWS from application code → AWS SDKs.

question: A company connects its on-premises data center to a VPC and runs some workloads in each location. Which deployment model is this?
explanations: A cloud-native deployment runs entirely in the cloud.
Hybrid deployments connect on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources.
Multi-Region describes how a cloud deployment is spread across Regions.
On-premises deployments don’t use the public cloud.
takeaway: Cloud + on-premises together → hybrid.

question: An administrator needs to change one setting on one S3 bucket, one time. Which access method is MOST appropriate?
options: A release pipeline in AWS CodePipeline
A custom application that uses an AWS SDK
explanations: The console is the quickest way to make a one-time change.
A pipeline automates repeated releases, not one setting change.
Writing code for one change is unnecessary.
Creating a template for a single change adds unnecessary work.
takeaway: One-off changes → console. Repeated tasks → automation.

question: Which service model gives a company control over the operating system of its servers while AWS manages the physical infrastructure?
options: Infrastructure as a service (IaaS), such as Amazon EC2
Function as a service, such as AWS Lambda
Platform as a service (PaaS), such as AWS Elastic Beanstalk
explanations: With IaaS, customers manage the OS and everything above it.
With SaaS, the customer just uses finished software.
With functions, AWS manages the operating system.
With PaaS, the provider manages the platform and runtime.
takeaway: Control of the OS on AWS hardware → IaaS (EC2).

question: Which TWO are benefits of infrastructure as code? (Select TWO.)
options: Templates remove the need for IAM permissions
Changes can be version-controlled and reviewed
Resources created from templates are free of charge
explanations: The same template produces the same resources every time.
Monitoring is still needed.
Creating resources still requires permissions.
Templates can be stored and reviewed like application code.
Resources are billed however they are created.
takeaway: IaC: consistent, repeatable, reviewable infrastructure.

question: What is an AWS Availability Zone?
options: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power and networking in a Region
A geographic area that contains several Regions
A data center in the customer’s own office
A location that caches content close to users
explanations: Each Region has multiple isolated Availability Zones.
A Region contains Availability Zones, not the reverse.
AWS Availability Zones are AWS facilities.
That describes an edge location.
takeaway: AZ = isolated data center(s) within a Region.

question: Which statement about AWS Regions is correct?
options: A Region is a single large data center
Each Region is a separate geographic area that contains multiple Availability Zones
New AWS services launch in all Regions on the same day
Data is copied between Regions automatically
explanations: A Region contains multiple AZs, each with one or more data centers.
Regions are isolated from each other and contain multiple AZs.
Service availability varies by Region.
Data stays in a Region unless the customer replicates it.
takeaway: Region = geographic area with multiple isolated AZs.

question: A company is choosing a Region for a new application. Which TWO factors should it consider? (Select TWO.)
options: The number of IAM users in the account
Distance from its users, for lower latency
The Region where the AWS account was created
The time zone of the account owner
explanations: IAM is global and doesn’t affect Region choice.
Closer Regions give users faster responses.
Laws may require data to stay in certain locations.
Accounts can use any Region.
The owner’s time zone isn’t a Region selection factor.
takeaway: Choose a Region by compliance, latency, services available, and cost.

question: What are AWS edge locations mainly used for?
options: Hosting the AWS Management Console for each country
Caching content and answering DNS queries close to users
Running EC2 instances in each city
explanations: Backups are stored in Regions.
The console isn’t hosted per edge location.
CloudFront and Route 53 use edge locations to reduce latency.
Edge locations don’t run your EC2 instances.
takeaway: Edge locations → CloudFront caching and Route 53 DNS near users.

question: How can a company make its application highly available within a single AWS Region?
options: Run larger instances in one Availability Zone
Deploy resources across multiple Availability Zones
Deploy the application to several edge locations
Turn on detailed monitoring for every instance
explanations: One AZ remains a single point of failure.
Multiple AZs remove single points of failure within a Region.
Edge locations deliver content; they don’t run the application.
Monitoring alone doesn’t increase availability.
takeaway: High availability in a Region → multiple AZs.

question: Why does deploying an application across multiple Availability Zones improve its resilience?
options: Each Availability Zone is located in a different Region
Availability Zones are physically separate and don’t share single points of failure such as power
Traffic between Availability Zones avoids the AWS network
Availability Zones automatically back up each other’s EBS volumes
explanations: AZs are within the same Region.
A problem in one AZ doesn’t take down the others.
AZs are connected by AWS’s own low-latency network.
EBS volumes aren’t automatically backed up across AZs.
takeaway: AZs are isolated: no shared single points of failure.

question: When should a company deploy its application in more than one AWS Region?
options: When it needs disaster recovery for a Regional outage or low latency for users on other continents
Whenever it needs to survive the failure of a single data center
When it wants to use the AWS Free Tier
When it uses more than one VPC
explanations: Multi-Region protects against Regional events and serves distant users.
Multiple AZs already protect against a data center failure.
Free Tier eligibility doesn’t depend on Regions.
Many VPCs can exist in one Region.
takeaway: Multi-Region → disaster recovery, global users, data sovereignty.

question: An application used by people in a large city needs single-digit millisecond latency, but the nearest AWS Region is far away. Which option fits BEST?
options: An additional Availability Zone in the distant Region
explanations: Local Zones place AWS compute and storage close to large population centers.
Direct Connect links a data center to AWS; it doesn’t move compute closer to users.
AZs are in the Region, so latency stays high.
Edge locations cache content; they don’t run application compute.
takeaway: AWS compute near a metro area → Local Zones.

question: Which AWS service provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud?
explanations: S3 is object storage.
EC2 provides virtual servers called instances.
ECS orchestrates containers.
Lambda runs functions without servers to manage.
takeaway: Virtual servers → EC2.

question: A company runs an in-memory analytics application that needs a large amount of RAM. Which EC2 instance family should it choose?
explanations: Accelerated computing instances add GPUs or other accelerators.
Compute optimized instances favor CPU.
Storage optimized instances favor local disk I/O.
Memory optimized instances are built for large in-memory datasets.
takeaway: Lots of RAM → memory optimized.

question: Which EC2 instance family is BEST for CPU-intensive workloads such as high-performance batch processing and scientific modeling?
explanations: Storage optimized instances favor disk I/O.
General purpose instances balance resources.
Compute optimized instances have high-performance processors.
Memory optimized instances favor RAM.
takeaway: CPU-bound → compute optimized.

question: A workload needs very high, sequential read and write access to large datasets on local storage. Which EC2 instance family fits BEST?
explanations: Memory optimized instances favor RAM.
Compute optimized instances favor CPU.
Storage optimized instances deliver high local disk throughput and IOPS.
General purpose instances balance resources.
takeaway: High local disk I/O → storage optimized.

question: A company wants to run code whenever a file is uploaded to Amazon S3, without managing servers, and pay only when the code runs. Which service should it use?
explanations: EC2 instances run and cost money even when idle.
Beanstalk runs web applications on EC2 instances.
Lightsail provides virtual servers with a monthly price.
Lambda runs code in response to events and charges per request and duration.
takeaway: Event-driven, serverless code → Lambda.

question: A team wants to run containers without managing the underlying EC2 instances. Which service should it use?
explanations: Outposts runs AWS infrastructure on premises.
ECR stores container images; it doesn’t run them.
Auto Scaling manages instance counts; you still manage the instances.
Fargate runs containers for ECS and EKS without servers to manage.
takeaway: Containers without managing servers → Fargate.

question: A company already runs its applications on Kubernetes on premises and wants a managed Kubernetes service on AWS. Which service should it use?
explanations: EKS runs the Kubernetes control plane for you.
ECR stores container images.
ECS is AWS’s own container orchestrator, not Kubernetes.
Beanstalk deploys applications, not Kubernetes clusters.
takeaway: Kubernetes → EKS.

question: Which service automatically adds or removes EC2 instances based on demand?
explanations: Auto Scaling adjusts the number of instances to demand.
CloudWatch alarms can trigger scaling, but they don’t launch instances.
Load balancers distribute traffic; they don’t add instances.
Compute Optimizer recommends instance sizes.
takeaway: Add or remove instances with demand → Auto Scaling.

question: What is the main purpose of Elastic Load Balancing?
options: Distributing incoming traffic across multiple targets
Adding instances when CPU utilization is high
explanations: Domain registration is done by Route 53.
Caching is done by CloudFront.
Load balancers spread traffic across healthy targets in several AZs.
Adding instances is Auto Scaling’s job.
takeaway: Distribute traffic across targets → Elastic Load Balancing.

question: A developer wants to deploy a Java web application quickly. AWS should handle provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring, but the developer wants to keep access to the underlying resources. Which service fits BEST?
explanations: Lightsail provides simple servers without managed scaling and load balancing for the app.
Lambda runs functions, not a traditional Java web application environment.
CloudFormation provisions what a template describes; it doesn’t manage the app environment.
Beanstalk manages the environment for your code while keeping the resources accessible.
takeaway: Upload code, AWS manages the environment (PaaS) → Elastic Beanstalk.

question: Which AWS service is a fully managed NoSQL key-value database?
explanations: Redshift is a data warehouse.
RDS runs relational databases.
DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL key-value and document database.
Aurora is a relational database.
takeaway: NoSQL key-value → DynamoDB.

question: A company needs a relational database that is compatible with MySQL and offers higher performance and availability than standard MySQL. Which service should it use?
explanations: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache.
Neptune is a graph database.
Aurora is MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible with higher performance and availability.
DynamoDB is a NoSQL database.
takeaway: MySQL-compatible, higher performance → Aurora.

question: Which service reduces read latency by caching frequently requested database results in memory?
explanations: ElastiCache serves cached data from memory in microseconds.
Redshift is a data warehouse.
Global tables replicate data across Regions.
Multi-AZ provides a standby for failover, not a cache.
takeaway: In-memory cache → ElastiCache.

explanations: RDS has less overhead than EC2.

EC2 gives full control for unsupported engines or OS-level needs.

question: A social network needs to store and query relationships between users, such as friends of friends. Which database service is designed for this?
explanations: DynamoDB is a key-value database; relationship queries are not its strength.
Relational databases struggle with deep relationship queries.

Neptune is a graph database for highly connected data.

Backups allow restores, not automatic failover.
Multi-AZ replicates synchronously to a standby and fails over automatically.

question: A company is migrating an Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Which TWO AWS services should it use? (Select TWO.)
explanations: DMS moves the data and replicates ongoing changes.

question: A company wants to move a MongoDB workload to a managed AWS database with minimal application changes. Which service should it choose?

Aurora is relational.
Neptune is a graph database.
DocumentDB is compatible with MongoDB APIs and drivers.

question: Which AWS service lets a company create a logically isolated virtual network?
explanations: A VPC is your own isolated network in AWS.
CloudFront is a content delivery network.
Direct Connect links your premises to AWS.
Route 53 is a DNS service.
takeaway: Isolated virtual network → Amazon VPC.

question: Which VPC component allows resources in a public subnet to communicate with the internet?
explanations: A NAT gateway gives private subnets outbound-only access.
A virtual private gateway terminates VPN connections.
An internet gateway connects the VPC to the internet.
Transit Gateway connects VPCs and networks.

question: Instances in a private subnet must download software updates from the internet but must not accept inbound connections from the internet. What should the company use?
options: An internet gateway attached to the private subnet
A security group that allows all inbound traffic
explanations: Routing to an internet gateway would make the subnet public.
This would expose the instances.
A NAT gateway allows outbound connections only.
Peering connects VPCs, not the internet.

question: Which statement about security groups is correct?
options: They are stateless and support deny rules
They require rules that allow return traffic explicitly
They are stateful and support allow rules only
They are applied at the subnet level
explanations: That describes network ACLs.
Return traffic is allowed automatically.
Security groups track connections and only allow traffic.
Security groups apply to instances and other resources.

question: A company needs to block traffic from a specific IP address range to every instance in a subnet. What should it use?
options: An IAM policy that denies the IP range
A security group with a deny rule
A route table entry for the IP range
A network ACL with a deny rule
explanations: IAM controls API access, not network traffic to instances.
Security groups can’t deny traffic.
Route tables direct traffic; they don’t filter it.
Network ACLs filter traffic at the subnet level and support deny rules.

question: Which AWS service provides DNS and domain name registration?
explanations: Route 53 is AWS’s DNS and domain registration service.
API Gateway manages APIs.
CloudFront delivers content.
VPC provides private networks.
takeaway: DNS and domains → Route 53.

question: A company needs a dedicated, private connection from its data center to AWS with consistent network performance. Which service should it use?
explanations: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private link with consistent performance.
Client VPN connects individual users.
A VPN runs over the internet, so performance can vary.
Global Accelerator speeds up user traffic to applications.
takeaway: Dedicated, consistent connection → Direct Connect.

question: A company needs to connect its office network to a VPC securely today, over the internet, at low cost. Which option should it choose?
explanations: CloudFront delivers content to users.
Direct Connect takes weeks to provision and costs more.
A Site-to-Site VPN can be set up quickly and encrypts traffic over the internet.
Transit Gateway is a hub; it still needs a VPN or Direct Connect to reach the office.
takeaway: Fast, low-cost encrypted link → Site-to-Site VPN.

question: Remote employees need secure access to internal applications in a VPC from their laptops. Which service should the company use?
explanations: Client VPN gives individual users encrypted access.
Site-to-Site VPN connects networks, not individual devices.
Direct Connect links a data center, not laptops.
Peering connects VPCs.
takeaway: Individual remote users → Client VPN.

question: Which option lets resources in a VPC reach supported AWS services privately, without an internet gateway or NAT gateway?
explanations: Transit Gateway connects networks; it doesn’t provide private service endpoints.
Interface endpoints keep traffic to AWS services on the AWS network.
Route 53 resolves names; it doesn’t change the network path.
Global Accelerator improves internet traffic to applications.
takeaway: Private access to AWS services from a VPC → PrivateLink endpoints.

question: Which AWS service provides object storage?
explanations: S3 stores objects in buckets.
EFS provides file storage.
EBS provides block storage.
Storage Gateway connects on-premises apps to cloud storage.
takeaway: Object storage → S3.

question: Which storage option provides persistent block storage for an EC2 instance?
explanations: EFS is a shared file system.
Instance store is block storage, but its data is lost when the instance stops.
EBS volumes persist independently of the instance.
S3 is object storage.
takeaway: Persistent block storage → EBS.

question: A fleet of Linux web servers needs to read and write the same files at the same time. Which service should the company use?
explanations: EFS is a shared file system that many instances can mount.
Glacier classes are for archives.
Instance store is local to one instance and temporary.
An EBS volume is attached to a single instance in most cases.
takeaway: Shared Linux file system → EFS.

question: A company needs Windows file shares that use the SMB protocol and integrate with Active Directory. Which service should it use?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explanations: FSx for Windows File Server provides SMB shares with Active Directory integration.
EBS is block storage for single instances.

EFS provides NFS for Linux.
takeaway: Windows SMB shares → FSx for Windows File Server.

question: Data in an S3 bucket has unknown and changing access patterns. Which storage class lowers cost without performance impact or operational overhead?
explanations: Standard is priced for frequently accessed data.
Deep Archive retrievals take hours.
One Zone-IA charges retrieval fees and keeps data in one AZ.
Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers automatically.
takeaway: Unknown access patterns → S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

explanations: Standard-IA is for data that needs immediate access.

Versioning keeps object versions; it doesn’t move objects between classes.
Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads over long distances.
Lifecycle rules transition objects between storage classes on a schedule.
takeaway: Move or expire objects over time → S3 Lifecycle.

question: An application needs temporary storage for cache and scratch data with very high I/O performance, and losing the data when the instance stops is acceptable. Which storage is the MOST cost-effective?

explanations: Provisioned IOPS volumes are persistent and cost extra.
EFS is shared network storage, not the fastest local scratch space.
S3 isn’t block storage for scratch data.
Instance store is fast local storage included in the instance price, but it is temporary.
takeaway: Fast, temporary scratch storage → instance store.

question: An on-premises application needs to store files in Amazon S3 while keeping a local cache of recently used files. Which service should the company use?
explanations: EFS is a cloud file system for AWS compute.
File Gateway presents S3 as a file share with a local cache.
Direct Connect provides a network link, not storage.
Backup manages backups, not file access with a cache.
takeaway: On-premises access to cloud storage with a local cache → Storage Gateway.

question: A company wants to manage backup schedules and retention for EBS volumes, RDS databases, and DynamoDB tables from one place. Which service should it use?
explanations: Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers for failover.
AWS Backup manages policy-based backups across many services.
Storage Gateway provides hybrid storage access.
Snapshots cover EBS only.

question: Which AWS service converts text into lifelike speech?

Polly turns text into speech.

Translate converts text between languages.

explanations: Rekognition analyzes images and video.

Textract extracts text and structured data from documents.
Translate translates text.

question: A company wants to analyze customer reviews to find out whether they are positive or negative. Which service should it use?
explanations: Polly converts text to speech.
Lex builds chatbots.
Rekognition analyzes images and video.
Comprehend detects sentiment and other insights in text.

explanations: Textract extracts data from documents.

explanations: Glue prepares data.

Kinesis ingests streaming data.
Athena runs SQL queries.
takeaway: BI dashboards → Quick Sight.

Step Functions orchestrates workflows.

SES sends email but doesn’t deliver to Lambda subscribers.

question: Which service stores container images so that Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS can deploy them?

Glacier classes archive data.

question: A university wants students to use one engineering desktop application through a web browser without installing it. Which service should it use?

question: Which option provides a relational database that automatically scales its capacity up and down with demand?

Network ACLs filter traffic at the subnet boundary.
takeaway: Where traffic goes → route table.

question: Which TWO statements about network ACLs are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: They evaluate every rule before deciding
They support both allow and deny rules
They are attached to individual instances
explanations: Rules are evaluated in number order, and the first match applies.
Network ACLs can explicitly deny traffic.
Return traffic must be allowed explicitly.
Network ACLs apply to subnets.
That is how security groups behave.
takeaway: Network ACLs: stateless, subnet level, allow and deny, ordered rules.

question: A company wants to connect 30 VPCs and two on-premises networks through one central hub. Which service should it use?
options: VPC peering between every pair of VPCs
explanations: Direct Connect links on-premises networks but isn’t a hub for VPCs.
Transit Gateway connects many VPCs and networks through one hub.
Route 53 provides DNS.
Peering many VPCs creates a complex mesh.
takeaway: Many VPCs + on-premises through a hub → Transit Gateway.

question: Which option sends users to the AWS Region that gives them the lowest latency, at the DNS level?
explanations: Load balancers distribute traffic within a Region.
Latency routing answers DNS queries with the lowest-latency Region.
CloudFront caches content; it isn’t DNS routing.
Peering connects VPCs.
takeaway: DNS routing to the lowest-latency Region → Route 53 latency routing.

question: Which Amazon Route 53 routing policy sends traffic to a standby site when health checks show the primary site is unhealthy?
explanations: Simple routing returns one answer without health-based failover.
Weighted routing splits traffic by percentage.
Geolocation routes by user location.
Failover routing switches to the standby when the primary is unhealthy.
takeaway: Active-passive DNS failover → failover routing.

question: Which service creates and manages APIs that front-end applications call to run AWS Lambda functions?
explanations: Route 53 provides DNS.
API Gateway exposes APIs that invoke Lambda and other backends.
CloudFront delivers content.
Global Accelerator routes network traffic.
takeaway: Managed APIs in front of Lambda → API Gateway.

question: A company wants to send 50% of its traffic to a new version of its website and 50% to the old version for testing. Which Route 53 routing policy should it use?
explanations: Weighted routing splits traffic by the weights you assign.
Simple routing can’t split traffic by percentage.
Latency routing chooses the fastest Region.
Failover is for active-passive setups.
takeaway: Split traffic by percentage → weighted routing.

question: A company uses AWS Direct Connect and wants a low-cost backup connection in case Direct Connect fails. What should it use?
options: AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
A second VPC in the same Region
explanations: Peering connects VPCs, not on-premises networks.
CloudFront delivers content to users.
A VPN is a common low-cost backup for Direct Connect.
Another VPC doesn’t connect the data center.
takeaway: Low-cost backup for Direct Connect → Site-to-Site VPN.

question: Which feature lets instances in two VPCs communicate using private IP addresses as if they were on the same network?
explanations: NAT gateways give private subnets outbound internet access.
Route 53 provides DNS.
Internet gateways connect a VPC to the internet.
Peering routes traffic privately between two VPCs.
takeaway: Private connection between two VPCs → VPC peering.

question: Which TWO are components of an Amazon VPC? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Route tables direct traffic in the VPC.
CloudFront is a separate service.
Subnets divide the VPC’s IP range.
IAM roles are identities, not network components.
Edge locations are part of the global infrastructure.
takeaway: VPC components: subnets, route tables, gateways, security groups, network ACLs.

question: A company’s website has users around the world. Which TWO services reduce latency for these users? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Transit Gateway connects VPCs.
Direct Connect links data centers, not end users.
NAT gateways provide outbound access for private subnets.
Global Accelerator routes users over the AWS network to the closest endpoint.
CloudFront serves cached content from nearby edge locations.
takeaway: Global user latency → CloudFront and Global Accelerator.

question: Which S3 storage class is designed for data accessed less than once a month that still needs millisecond access and must survive the loss of an Availability Zone?
explanations: Standard-IA stores data across multiple AZs with millisecond access.
Deep Archive retrievals take hours.
Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours.
One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ.
takeaway: Infrequent, immediate access, multi-AZ → S3 Standard-IA.

question: Which S3 storage class keeps data in a single Availability Zone at a lower price, for infrequently accessed data that can be recreated?
explanations: Standard stores data across multiple AZs.
One Zone-IA uses one AZ to lower the price.
Intelligent-Tiering stores data across multiple AZs.
Glacier Instant Retrieval stores data across multiple AZs.
takeaway: Re-creatable, infrequent data → S3 One Zone-IA.

question: A hospital stores medical images that are accessed about once a quarter but must be available within milliseconds. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective?
explanations: Standard costs more for rarely accessed data.
Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours.
Deep Archive retrievals take hours.
It offers archive pricing with millisecond retrieval.
takeaway: Rarely accessed but needed instantly → Glacier Instant Retrieval.

question: What does S3 Versioning help protect against?
options: High storage costs for old data
Accidental deletion or overwriting of objects
explanations: Upload speed isn’t affected by versioning.
Versioning can increase storage costs.
DDoS protection comes from Shield.
Earlier versions can be restored.
takeaway: Recover from deletes and overwrites → S3 Versioning.

question: Which TWO statements describe how Amazon EBS volumes and snapshots work? (Select TWO.)
options: EBS is object storage accessed over HTTP
An EBS volume is tied to a single Availability Zone
EBS snapshots can be used to create volumes in other AZs
EBS volumes are shared by thousands of instances at once
Data on EBS is lost when an instance stops
explanations: EBS is block storage.
Volumes attach to instances in the same AZ.
Snapshots are stored regionally.
EBS volumes typically attach to one instance.
EBS data persists; instance store data is lost.
takeaway: EBS: block storage in one AZ; snapshots move data across AZs.

question: Which service provides a fully managed NetApp ONTAP file system for enterprise file workloads?
options: Amazon S3 with S3 File Gateway
explanations: EBS is block storage.
FSx for NetApp ONTAP runs ONTAP as a managed service.
EFS is a native NFS file system for Linux.
File Gateway gives on-premises access to S3.
takeaway: Managed ONTAP file systems → FSx for NetApp ONTAP.

question: A company wants to replace the physical backup tapes in its data center with cloud storage without changing its backup software. Which option should it use?
options: Amazon EFS with infrequent access storage
Amazon EBS snapshots of on-premises disks
explanations: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads; it doesn’t emulate tapes.
EFS isn’t a tape replacement for backup software.
Tape Gateway presents virtual tapes to existing backup software and stores them in S3.
EBS snapshots back up EBS volumes, not on-premises tapes.
takeaway: Replace tapes without changing backup software → Tape Gateway.

question: A company needs its critical on-premises servers running in AWS within minutes if its data center fails. Which service should it use?
explanations: It replicates servers continuously and launches them in AWS on failover.
Storage Gateway provides hybrid storage.
AWS Backup restores data but isn’t built for minutes-level server failover.
Glacier classes are for archives.
takeaway: Fail servers over to AWS within minutes → Elastic Disaster Recovery.

question: Which S3 feature automatically deletes log files 365 days after they are created?
explanations: Versioning keeps object versions.
Block Public Access controls public access.
Lifecycle rules can expire objects after a set number of days.
Object Lock prevents deletion for a retention period.
takeaway: Delete objects after a set time → Lifecycle expiration.

question: A front-end developer wants to host a React web app with Git-based deployments and add user sign-in quickly. Which service should the developer use?
explanations: Beanstalk deploys server-side applications on EC2.
CloudFront delivers content but doesn’t build and deploy apps.
Lightsail provides simple servers.
Amplify hosts web apps with Git-based deployments and adds features such as authentication.
takeaway: Front-end web and mobile apps → Amplify.

question: An EC2 instance keeps important data on its instance store volume. What happens to that data when the instance is stopped?
options: It is kept until the instance is terminated
It is backed up to Amazon S3 automatically
It is moved to an EBS volume automatically
explanations: It is lost when the instance stops.
Instance store is temporary; persistent data belongs on EBS or S3.
There is no automatic backup.
Instance store data isn’t moved anywhere.
takeaway: Instance store data is lost when an instance stops.

question: A company must keep copies of its RDS database and EFS file system backups in a second Region, managed centrally. What should it use?
options: S3 Versioning on a central bucket
Amazon EBS snapshots of each instance
explanations: Backup plans can copy backups to another Region.
Versioning doesn’t back up RDS or EFS.
EBS snapshots don’t cover RDS or EFS centrally.
Load balancing distributes traffic.
takeaway: Central backups with copies in another Region → AWS Backup.

question: Which service detects objects, faces, and inappropriate content in images and videos?
explanations: Rekognition analyzes images and video.
Comprehend analyzes text.
Polly converts text to speech.
Textract extracts text from documents.
takeaway: Images and video → Rekognition.

question: A contact center wants to convert recorded customer calls into text for analysis. Which service should it use?
explanations: Translate converts text between languages.
Transcribe converts speech to text.
Lex builds chatbots.
Polly converts text to speech.
takeaway: Speech → text: Transcribe.

question: A company wants to translate its product descriptions into several languages automatically. Which service should it use?
explanations: Polly converts text to speech.
Transcribe converts speech to text.
Comprehend analyzes text.
Translate provides machine translation.
takeaway: Translate text → Amazon Translate.

question: Which service prepares, transforms, and catalogs data with serverless ETL jobs and crawlers?
explanations: Kinesis ingests streaming data.
Glue provides serverless ETL and the Data Catalog.
Redshift is a data warehouse.
Athena queries data; it isn’t an ETL service.
takeaway: Serverless ETL + Data Catalog → Glue.

question: A company processes petabytes of data with Apache Spark and Hadoop. Which service is designed for this?
explanations: EMR runs big data frameworks such as Spark and Hadoop.
Quick Sight builds dashboards.
Athena runs SQL queries on S3.
Lambda runs short functions.
takeaway: Spark or Hadoop → EMR.

question: Which AWS offering is a generative AI assistant that helps developers write, explain, and upgrade code and answers questions about their AWS resources?
explanations: Lex builds intent-based chatbots.
Amazon Q Developer is the generative AI assistant for building on AWS. (Amazon Q Business closed to new customers in July 2026; Amazon Quick is its successor.)
Comprehend analyzes text.
SageMaker AI is for building your own models.
takeaway: Generative AI assistant for code and AWS → Amazon Q (Q Developer).

question: Which TWO services can query or process data in Amazon S3 without the company managing servers? (Select TWO.)
explanations: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache.
Glue runs serverless ETL jobs on S3 data.
EMR on EC2 runs clusters that the company manages.
Provisioned clusters must be sized and managed.
Athena runs serverless SQL on S3.
takeaway: Serverless analytics on S3 → Athena and Glue.

question: A company wants to search and analyze application logs with dashboards in near real time. Which service should it use?
explanations: Athena runs ad hoc SQL on S3, not near-real-time dashboards.
Redshift is a data warehouse for structured analytics.
Glue prepares data.
OpenSearch provides log analytics and dashboards.
takeaway: Search and log analytics → OpenSearch Service.

question: Which service coordinates a multi-step order workflow across Lambda functions, with retries and error handling?
explanations: EventBridge routes events but doesn’t manage multi-step state.
SNS pushes messages to subscribers.
SQS queues messages between components.
Step Functions orchestrates workflows as state machines.
takeaway: Multi-step workflows with state → Step Functions.

question: Which TWO services help developers build, test, and release code automatically? (Select TWO.)
explanations: CodeBuild compiles and tests code.
CodePipeline automates the release process.
X-Ray traces requests in running applications.
CloudTrail records API activity.
Config records resource configurations.
takeaway: Build and test → CodeBuild. Release automation → CodePipeline.

question: Which TWO AWS services are global services rather than services that run in one AWS Region? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Databases run in a Region, optionally across AZs.
Route 53 public DNS is a global service.
Instances run in a specific AZ of a Region.
A load balancer runs in one Region and spreads traffic across its AZs.
CloudFront serves content from edge locations worldwide.
takeaway: Global: IAM, Route 53, CloudFront, Global Accelerator. Regional: EC2, ELB, RDS, VPC.

question: Which statement correctly compares Availability Zones with edge locations?
options: Edge locations keep standby copies of RDS databases for failover
Edge locations run Amazon EC2 instances close to users
AZs are spread across several continents so that each Region can serve global users with lower latency
AZs run instances and databases; edge locations cache content near users
explanations: RDS standbys run in another AZ of the same Region.
Edge locations host CloudFront and Route 53, not EC2 instances.
All of a Region’s AZs are in the same geographic area.
AZs hold your resources in a Region; edge locations deliver content and DNS answers close to users.
takeaway: AZs = where resources run, inside a Region. Edge locations = content delivery and DNS near users.

question: Which TWO statements about connecting on-premises networks to AWS are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: Amazon Connect provides a private, dedicated network link between a company’s offices and its VPCs on AWS
AWS Client VPN connects an entire data center router to a VPC
AWS Site-to-Site VPN encrypts traffic between an on-premises network and a VPC over the internet
Amazon CloudFront encrypts traffic between branch offices and a VPC
AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private link that doesn’t use the public internet
explanations: Amazon Connect is a contact center service; the network link is Direct Connect.
Client VPN connects individual users’ devices.
Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec tunnels over an existing internet connection.
CloudFront delivers content to users; it isn’t a network connection.
Direct Connect gives consistent performance over a private connection.
takeaway: Encrypted over the internet → Site-to-Site VPN. Dedicated and private → Direct Connect. Individual users → Client VPN.

question: A retailer needs a private, dedicated network connection from its data center to AWS. It also wants to run its customer service phone lines from a cloud contact center. Which TWO services should it use? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Client VPN connects individual remote users over the internet.
Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center.
Direct Connect is the dedicated network link.
SNS sends notifications.
Lex builds chatbots and voice bots; it can be added to a contact center but doesn’t run one.
takeaway: Direct Connect = network link. Amazon Connect = contact center.

question: A company hosts its marketing website as static files in one Amazon S3 bucket in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. Visitors in Australia report slow page loads. Which change will MOST improve their experience?
options: Add a Route 53 latency-based routing record for the bucket
Serve the bucket through Amazon CloudFront
Add DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the bucket
Move the files to the S3 One Zone-IA storage class
explanations: With one bucket there is one endpoint, so latency routing has nothing to choose between.
CloudFront caches the files at edge locations near visitors.
DAX is a cache for DynamoDB tables, not for S3 or websites.
A storage class changes cost and resilience, not the distance to users.
takeaway: Static content for distant users → CloudFront.

question: A language-learning app must read each lesson aloud to students and convert the students’ spoken answers into text for grading. Which TWO services should it use? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Textract extracts text from scanned documents.
Translate converts text between languages.
Comprehend finds meaning, such as sentiment, in text.
Transcribe turns speech into text.
Polly turns text into speech.
takeaway: Text → speech: Polly. Speech → text: Transcribe.

question: An order system needs SQL joins across customer, order, and product tables, with AWS handling database patching. Which TWO services can host this database? (Select TWO.)
explanations: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache.
Neptune is a graph database.
Aurora is a managed relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.
DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value database without SQL joins.
RDS runs managed relational database engines.
takeaway: Relational (SQL, joins) → RDS or Aurora. NoSQL key-value → DynamoDB.

question: A company will store millions of product images that its website and mobile app read over HTTPS. Which TWO characteristics of Amazon S3 make it a good fit? (Select TWO.)
options: It keeps data until the instance that uses it stops
It attaches to one EC2 instance as its boot volume
It is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) of durability
It must be mounted as a network file system before applications can read it
It stores each image as an object with a key and metadata
explanations: That describes instance store.
Boot volumes are EBS block storage.
S3 stores objects redundantly across devices and AZs.
Network file systems are EFS or FSx; S3 is read over HTTPS.
S3 is object storage reached through APIs and URLs.
takeaway: S3 = durable object storage over HTTPS. EFS = shared file system. EBS = block volume.

question: A team is choosing storage for a fleet of Linux web servers, including their boot volumes and shared content. Which TWO statements about AWS storage are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: Amazon EFS provides SMB file shares for Windows applications
Instance store volumes keep their data after the instance is stopped and started again
An Amazon EBS volume provides block storage in one Availability Zone
Amazon S3 buckets are attached to instances as block devices
Many Linux instances can mount the same Amazon EFS file system at once
explanations: EFS uses NFS for Linux; SMB shares come from FSx for Windows File Server.
Instance store data is lost when the instance stops.
EBS volumes live in one AZ and attach to instances there.
S3 is object storage accessed through APIs.
EFS is a shared NFS file system.
takeaway: EFS = shared NFS. EBS = block in one AZ. Instance store = temporary. FSx for Windows = SMB.

question: When a payment fails, an order service must alert the on-call team by email and SMS. It must also hold new orders until the warehouse system is ready to process them. Which TWO services should it use? (Select TWO.)
explanations: SNS pushes notifications to email, SMS, and other subscribers.
EventBridge routes events to targets such as SNS; it doesn’t deliver email or SMS itself.
SES sends email but not SMS, and it doesn’t queue work for consumers.
SQS queues messages until consumers are ready.
Amazon Connect is a contact center service.
takeaway: Notify people → SNS. Buffer work until consumers are ready → SQS.

question: Which TWO statements about Elastic Load Balancing are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: It caches static content at edge locations
One load balancer distributes incoming traffic to targets in several AWS Regions around the world
It runs health checks and stops routing traffic to unhealthy targets
A load balancer can route traffic to targets in several AZs within its Region
It launches new EC2 instances when CPU utilization is high
explanations: That is CloudFront.
Load balancers are Regional; use Route 53 or Global Accelerator across Regions.
Health checks keep traffic away from failed targets.
Spreading targets across AZs is how ELB adds availability.
That is EC2 Auto Scaling.
takeaway: ELB: one Region, many AZs, health checks. Across Regions → Route 53 or Global Accelerator.

question: Which TWO workloads are a good fit for AWS Lambda functions? (Select TWO.)
options: An API handler that runs in under a second, a few thousand times a day
Creating a thumbnail each time an image is uploaded to Amazon S3
Archiving petabytes of records for seven years
A licensed application that must run on a dedicated physical server with visible sockets and cores
Virtual desktops that employees use all day
explanations: You pay per request and duration, with nothing to run between calls.
Short, event-driven code is Lambda’s main use case.
Long-term archives belong in S3 Glacier storage classes.
Per-server licensing needs EC2 Dedicated Hosts.
Virtual desktops come from Amazon WorkSpaces.
takeaway: Lambda functions: short, event-driven code with no servers to manage.

question: A gaming company’s DynamoDB table receives the same read requests millions of times a minute. It needs microsecond read latency with minimal application changes. Which option fits BEST?
explanations: CloudFront caches web content at the edge, not DynamoDB reads inside an application.
Global Accelerator improves network paths to endpoints; it doesn’t cache data.
Global tables replicate data across Regions; they don’t add an in-memory cache.
DAX is an in-memory cache built for DynamoDB that needs few code changes.
takeaway: Microsecond reads for DynamoDB → DAX. Global Accelerator speeds up networking, not data.

question: Analysts want to run SQL queries on log files in Amazon S3 without managing servers, and share the results with executives as interactive dashboards. Which TWO services should they use? (Select TWO.)
explanations: Athena runs serverless SQL queries on data in S3.
Kinesis ingests streaming data.
Quick Sight builds interactive BI dashboards.
EMR on EC2 can run SQL, but the company would manage the clusters.
ElastiCache is an in-memory cache.
takeaway: Serverless SQL on S3 → Athena. Dashboards → Quick Sight.

question: Which EC2 purchasing option is BEST for a short-term workload with unpredictable usage that must not be interrupted?
explanations: Dedicated Hosts are for licensing or compliance needs.
Reserved Instances need a 1- or 3-year commitment.
Spot Instances can be interrupted.
On-Demand has no commitment and isn’t interrupted.
takeaway: Short-term, unpredictable, uninterruptible → On-Demand.

question: A company runs a database server 24 hours a day and plans to keep it for three years. Which purchasing option gives the LARGEST discount?
options: A 3-year Standard Reserved Instance paid All Upfront
A 1-year Convertible Reserved Instance with No Upfront payment
explanations: Spot Instances can be interrupted, which a database can’t tolerate.
The longest term, Standard type, and full upfront payment give the biggest discount.
A shorter term, Convertible type, and no upfront payment give a smaller discount.
On-Demand has the highest price.
takeaway: Steady usage: longer term + more upfront = bigger discount.

question: Which workload is the BEST fit for EC2 Spot Instances?
options: A licensed application tied to a physical server
A production database that must stay online
A checkout service with steady traffic around the clock
Batch image processing that can restart if it is interrupted
explanations: This needs Dedicated Hosts.
Interruptions would take the database offline.
Steady, critical workloads fit Reserved Instances or Savings Plans.
Spot suits flexible, fault-tolerant work.
takeaway: Interruptible, flexible work → Spot.

question: A company wants to commit to a consistent amount of compute spend for one year and have the discount apply automatically across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda. Which option should it choose?
explanations: EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply to one instance family in one Region.
Reserved Instances apply only to matching EC2 usage.
Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda.
Spot isn’t a commitment-based discount.
takeaway: Flexible commitment across EC2, Fargate, Lambda → Compute Savings Plans.

question: What is the main difference between Standard and Convertible Reserved Instances?
options: Standard Reserved Instances don’t require a term commitment
Convertible Reserved Instances also cover Lambda and Fargate
Standard Reserved Instances can be canceled at any time
Convertible RIs can be exchanged for other instance families, for a smaller discount
explanations: Both types require a 1- or 3-year term.
That describes Compute Savings Plans.
Both types are a commitment for the full term.
Flexibility to change attributes costs some of the discount.
takeaway: Convertible = more flexibility, smaller discount.

question: A company must make sure EC2 capacity is available in a specific Availability Zone for a product launch next week, without a long-term commitment. Which option should it use?
explanations: Spot capacity isn’t guaranteed.
Dedicated Instances change tenancy, not capacity guarantees.
Savings Plans give discounts but don’t reserve capacity.
Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity in an AZ for any duration.
takeaway: Guarantee capacity in an AZ, no long commitment → Capacity Reservations.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations with consolidated billing. One account bought Reserved Instances that it no longer fully uses, and another account runs matching instances. What happens?
options: The other account must buy its own Reserved Instances to get a discount
The unused Reserved Instances are refunded at the end of the month
The unused Reserved Instance discount can apply to the matching usage in the other account
The Reserved Instances move permanently to the account with the most usage
explanations: Discount sharing lets it benefit without buying.
Reserved Instances aren’t refunded.
RI discounts are shared across accounts in the organization by default.
Ownership doesn’t change; the discount is applied on the bill.
takeaway: Consolidated billing shares RI and Savings Plans discounts.

question: Which type of data transfer is generally free of charge?
options: Data transferred into AWS from the internet
Data transferred out of Amazon S3 to the internet
Data transferred out from EC2 to the internet
explanations: Inbound data transfer is free.
Inter-Region transfer is charged.
Data transfer out to the internet is charged.
Data transfer out to the internet is charged.
takeaway: Inbound → free. Outbound and between Regions → charged.

question: Compliance rules require a company’s instances to run on hardware that no other AWS customer uses. The company doesn’t need visibility of physical cores or sockets. Which option is the MOST cost-effective?
explanations: Dedicated Hosts give a whole server and core visibility, which costs more than needed here.
Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware without paying for a whole host.
Spot runs on shared hardware and can be interrupted.
Shared tenancy doesn’t meet the requirement.
takeaway: Single-tenant hardware without core visibility → Dedicated Instances.

question: Which TWO factors affect what a company pays for Amazon S3? (Select TWO.)
options: Data transferred out of S3 to the internet
The AWS Region where the account was created
The number of IAM users who can access the bucket
The storage class and the amount of data stored
Data uploaded into S3 from the internet
explanations: Data transfer out is charged per GB.
Account creation location doesn’t affect pricing.
IAM users don’t affect S3 charges.
Storage is priced per GB and varies by class.
Inbound data transfer is free.
takeaway: S3 cost: storage (by class) + requests + retrieval + data transfer out.

question: Which AWS tool estimates the monthly cost of an architecture before it is deployed?
explanations: The Pricing Calculator models the cost of planned resources.
Budgets alerts on spending against a limit.
Cost Explorer analyzes costs that have already happened.
Cost and Usage Reports provide detailed historical billing data.
takeaway: Estimate before building → Pricing Calculator.

question: Which service sends an alert when actual or forecasted costs exceed an amount that the company sets?
explanations: Cost Explorer visualizes and forecasts costs but doesn’t send threshold alerts.
These reports provide detailed data, not alerts.
The Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deployment.
Budgets notifies you when spend crosses a threshold.
takeaway: Alert on spending thresholds → AWS Budgets.

question: A manager wants to see which services caused last month’s increase in AWS spending and view a forecast for next month. Which tool should the manager use?
explanations: Cost Explorer shows costs by service over time and forecasts future spend.
The Pricing Calculator estimates planned costs.
Budgets tracks spending against limits.
Trusted Advisor recommends savings but doesn’t analyze trends.
takeaway: Analyze past spend and forecast → Cost Explorer.

question: A company wants to track its AWS costs by department. What should it do?
options: Turn on AWS Config in each department’s resources
Create a separate IAM user for each department
Tag resources with a department tag and activate it as a cost allocation tag
Use the Pricing Calculator for each department
explanations: Config tracks configurations, not costs.
IAM users don’t organize costs.
Activated tags let you group costs by department.
The calculator estimates costs; it doesn’t track actual spend.
takeaway: Costs by department or project → cost allocation tags.

question: Which AWS billing feature provides the most detailed, line-item cost and usage data that can be analyzed with Amazon Athena?
explanations: Cost Explorer shows summarized views, not every line item.
Budgets tracks spending against limits.
The dashboard summarizes charges.
Cost and Usage Reports deliver line-item data to S3 for analysis.
takeaway: Most granular billing data → Cost and Usage Reports.

question: Which TWO are benefits of consolidated billing in AWS Organizations? (Select TWO.)
options: Free AWS Support for member accounts
Automatic Reserved Instance purchases for steady workloads
One bill for all accounts in the organization
Combined usage that reaches volume pricing discounts sooner
explanations: Billing doesn’t delete resources.
Support plans are still charged.
Consolidated billing shares discounts but never buys commitments for you.
The management account pays for all member accounts.
Usage is aggregated across accounts for tiered pricing.
takeaway: Consolidated billing: one bill + volume discounts + shared RIs/Savings Plans.

question: Where can a company see its current bill, its invoices, and the credits applied to its account?
options: The AWS Billing and Cost Management console
explanations: The Health Dashboard shows service events.
The billing console shows bills, invoices, payments, and credits.
Trusted Advisor provides recommendations.
Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.
takeaway: Bills, invoices, credits → Billing and Cost Management console.

question: Which AWS Support plan includes a designated technical account manager (TAM)?
explanations: Enterprise Support includes a designated TAM.
Professional Services is a consulting offering, not a support plan.
Business Support+ gives 24/7 support engineers but no designated TAM.
Basic Support includes account and billing help only.
takeaway: Designated TAM → Enterprise Support (or Unified Operations).

question: Which of the following is included with AWS Basic Support at no cost?
options: Technical support cases with a 30-minute response
The full set of Trusted Advisor checks
Customer service for account and billing questions
explanations: Technical cases need a paid plan.
Basic includes only the core checks.
A TAM comes with Enterprise Support.
